title: Geometric Frobenius acts on the Tate twist Lambda(m) by q^{-m}
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, $q=p^a$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ in $\Qlb$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\geq1$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$. Take $Y_0=\Spec k_0$, so $Y=s=\Spec k$ and $g_s=\Spec(\gamma):s\to s$ with $\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q$ the geometric Frobenius. Let $\Lambda(m)_s$, $m\in\mathbf Z$, be the Tate twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and $\theta_m:Lg_s^*\Lambda(m)_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(m)_s$ their canonical Weil structures [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. Let

$$
 F_m:\RGamma(s,\Lambda(m)_s)\xrightarrow{\ \tau\ }\RGamma(s,Lg_s^*\Lambda(m)_s)\xrightarrow{\RGamma(\theta_m)}\RGamma(s,\Lambda(m)_s)
$$

be the geometric Frobenius endomorphism, $\tau$ being the transport of cohomology along $g_s$ [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] and $\RGamma$, $H^i$ the cohomology of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Then $H^i(s,\Lambda(m)_s)=0$ for $i\neq0$, $H^0(s,\Lambda(m)_s)$ is free of rank one over $\Lambda$, and $H^0(F_m)$ is multiplication by $q^{-m}$, where $q\in\mathbf Z_\ell^\times$ (as $\ell\neq p$) and $q^{-m}$ acts through $\mathbf Z_\ell\to\Lambda$. In particular geometric Frobenius acts on $\Lambda(1)$ by $q^{-1}$, on $\Lambda(m)$ by $q^{-m}$ and on $\Lambda(-d)$ by $q^{d}$ ($d\geq0$), for $\Lambda=E$ and $\Lambda=\Qlb$ (where this is the action of the global geometric Frobenius $F$ of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] on $H^0(s,E(m)_s)$, resp. its scalar extension to $\Qlb$). These scalars are compatible with finite reduction and scalar extension: the reduction isomorphism $H^0(s,\mathcal O_E(m)_s)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\cong H^0(s,A_{E,n}(m)_s)$, the isomorphism $H^0(s,\mathcal O_E(m)_s)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\cong H^0(s,E(m)_s)$ and the scalar-extension isomorphisms to $E'\supseteq E$ and to $\Qlb$ intertwine the operators $H^0(F_m)$.

proof.text: Choose compatible primitive roots $\zeta_r\in\mu_{\ell^r}(k)$, $\zeta_{r+1}^{\ell}=\zeta_r$: the cyclicity and orders in [lem-pur-frobenius-roots-of-unity-power] give a primitive $\zeta_1$, and an $\ell$-th root of $\zeta_r$ exists in the algebraically closed field $k$ and has order $\ell^{r+1}$. These choices trivialize the sheaves [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf] on $s$, not just their groups of global sections. Indeed, for a section $u$ on any $U\to s$, the factorization $X^{\ell^r}-1=\prod_{j=0}^{\ell^r-1}(X-\zeta_r^j)$ has pairwise unit differences. The Lagrange expressions $e_j=\prod_{i\ne j}(u-\zeta_r^i)/(\zeta_r^j-\zeta_r^i)$ satisfy $e_je_i=0$ for $i\ne j$, $e_j^2=e_j$, $\sum e_j=1$, and $(u-\zeta_r^j)e_j=0$; these identities follow by reducing polynomial identities modulo $X^{\ell^r}-1$. The clopen pieces $D(e_j)$ therefore cover $U$ and on them $u=\zeta_r^j$. The unique label $j$ gives the inverse of $(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_s\to\mu_{\ell^r,s}$, $j\mapsto\zeta_r^j$, as sheaves. The transitions are reduction of labels since $(\zeta_{r+1}^j)^\ell=\zeta_r^j$. Taking the sectionwise inverse limit [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] gives $\Zl(1)_s\cong\widehat{\Zl}_s$, with generator $e=(\zeta_r)_r$.

The completed coefficient identification and reduction in [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], clause 3, turn the preceding trivialization into $\mathcal O_E(1)_s\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}$ and $A_{E,n}(1)_s\cong(A_{E,n})_s$, with generators $e_{\mathcal O_E}=e\otimes1$ and $e_A=e_{\mathcal O_E}\otimes1$. For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E,A_{E,n}$, [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] now identifies $\Lambda(m)_s$ with the free coefficient sheaf on $e_m=e_\Lambda^{\otimes m}$ for $m>0$, on $e_0=1$ for $m=0$, and on the dual generator $e_{-r}$ defined by $e_{-r}(e_r)=1$ for $r>0$. The tensor and Hom identifications have explicit inverses $a e_r\mapsto a$ and $\varphi\mapsto\varphi(e_r)$; no commutation of arbitrary sheaf Hom with sections is being assumed. The sections of the coefficient sheaves are $A_{E,n}$ and $\mathcal O_E$. For the finite constant sheaf, a section over the terminal object $s$ is represented after sheafification by compatible labels in $A_{E,n}$ on a pro-etale cover of $s$; the equalizer condition on every pairwise fibre product forces all nonempty labels to agree (a product of two nonempty schemes over the field $k$ is nonempty), and a single label gives such a section. Hence $\Gamma(s,(A_{E,n})_s)=A_{E,n}$. For the integral object use [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction] with $X=s$, identifying the completed sheaf with continuous $\mathcal O_E$-valued functions, whose sections on the one-point space $|s|$ are $\mathcal O_E$. Here $s$ is noetherian. Thus $\Gamma(s,\Lambda(m)_s)$ is free of rank one with generator $e_m$.

source.place: Tate-twist construction and finite reduction; completed integral coefficients on the geometric point

proof.text: For $Y=s$ the structure morphism $a_Y$ is the identity, so the definition [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] gives $\RGamma(s,M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(M)$. By [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], for a sheaf placed in degree zero this is its sections in degree zero, with no higher or negative cohomology. Apply this to the finite and integral free lines just constructed. At rational coefficients [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] computes the fiber of the integral representative by termwise tensor with $E$, and at algebraically closed coefficients it uses the common finite stage. In each case the result is the free rank-one $\Lambda$-module in degree zero. This proves both assertions about $H^i$, without treating a pro-etale topos as the category of sets or using an unproved equivalence of coefficient categories.

source.place: (2.2), pp. 280-281; exact evaluation and the coefficient fiber definitions

proof.text: Identify the operator specified in the statement, rather than only an abstract Galois action. The ordinary transport [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] for $a_Y=\operatorname{id}_s$ is the point transport: the mate formula in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] is the identity exchange after the identity direct-image identifications, since its unit and counit are identities. By [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] the point transport is $\Gamma(s,\kappa_M)\circ\sigma_M$, where $\sigma_M$ is restriction along $g_s:(s,g_s)\to(s,\operatorname{id})$ followed by the inverse-image coprojection. The Weil structure [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists] is $\tau_m^\Lambda\circ\lambda_M$. On these free lines the canonical identification $\lambda_M$ of [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] cancels $\kappa_M$: at finite level, the comparison [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] sends $x$ to $x\otimes1$, and the identification sends $x\otimes a$ to $c_\Lambda^{-1}(a)x$. At integral level, the displayed construction of $\kappa$ in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] has, after reduction to each $A_{E,r}$, the coordinate map $x\mapsto x\otimes1$; the canonical identification back to the inverse-image line sends $x\otimes a$ to $c_{A_{E,r}}^{-1}(a)x$. These coordinate composites are $x$ and commute with the reduction transitions, so the induced composite on the completed inverse-limit model is the identity. Consequently $H^0(F_m)=\Gamma(s,\tau_m^\Lambda)\circ\sigma_{\Lambda(m)}$ for $\Lambda=A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E$. In particular the constant coefficient transport followed by $c_\Lambda$ fixes every scalar: restriction of a constant section is the same section, and for completed coefficients this holds at every quotient. This calculation also shows that restriction and the inverse-image coprojection send tensor generators to tensor generators and commute with evaluation of a dual on its generator.

source.place: (1.1.7), pp. 150-151, transport of structure; explicit point transport and canonical pullback comparisons

proof.text: At level $\mu_{\ell^r}$, the restriction in $\sigma$ is pullback of units along $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, and hence sends $\zeta\in k^\times$ to $\gamma(\zeta)$. The roots-of-unity inverse-image comparison of [lem-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image-iso], clause 3, is the identity on the roots of unity of the unchanged underlying scheme at the object $(s,g_s)$, so it introduces no further field automorphism. Clause 1 of that lemma gives compatibility with $\zeta\mapsto\zeta^\ell$. By [lem-pur-frobenius-roots-of-unity-power], clauses 2 and 3, $\gamma(\zeta)=\zeta^{q'}$ with $qq'\equiv1\pmod{\ell^r}$, and on $T_\ell\mu(k)$ the resulting operator is multiplication by $q^{-1}\in\mathbf Z_\ell^\times$. The limit in the canonical Weil structure [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists], clause 2, is exactly this componentwise action. Thus the composite on $\Zl(1)$ sends $e$ to $q^{-1}e$; it is geometric, not arithmetic, Frobenius.

source.place: (2.2), pp. 280-281, arithmetic Frobenius acts by q; Weil II (1.1.7), geometric Frobenius is its inverse

proof.text: Use the formulas defining $\tau_1^{\mathcal O_E}$ and $\tau_1^{A_{E,n}}$ in [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists], clause 2. Their coefficient factors fix $1$ by step 4, so $F_1(e_\Lambda)=q^{-1}e_\Lambda$ for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E,A_{E,n}$. Clause 3 defines $\tau_m^\Lambda$ for positive $m$ by tensor powers. Starting with $m=1$, if $F_m(e_m)=q^{-m}e_m$, then $F_{m+1}(e_m\otimes e_\Lambda)=(q^{-m}e_m)\otimes(q^{-1}e_\Lambda)=q^{-(m+1)}e_{m+1}$. This proves the assertion for every $m>0$. The operator is $\Lambda$-linear since the restriction/comparison on the coefficient factor fixes scalars, so the equation on a generator determines it on the whole module.

source.place: The clauses for E(1), E(m), and finite reduction, proved first on the integral and finite lines

proof.text: For $m=0$, clause 3 of [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists] uses the constant coefficient structure, so step 4 gives $F_0(1)=1=q^0$. For $m=-r<0$, that clause defines the dual structure by $\varphi\mapsto c_\Lambda\circ\varphi\circ(\tau_r^\Lambda)^{-1}$. Together with the evaluation compatibility in step 4, this is the contragredient of the operator $F_r$ computed in step 6. Explicitly, $F_{-r}(e_{-r})(e_r)=e_{-r}(F_r^{-1}e_r)=e_{-r}(q^r e_r)=q^r$. Hence $F_{-r}=q^r\operatorname{id}$, giving $q^{-m}$ for all integers $m$. Invertibility of $q$ is essential here and holds since $q=p^a$ and $\ell\ne p$.

source.place: (2.2), p. 280, negative twists are dual tensor powers

proof.text: Finite reduction of the integral generator sends $e_{\mathcal O_E}$ to $e_A$. The tensor/dual definitions [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] therefore send $e_m\otimes1$ to $e_{m,A}$ for every integer $m$: for negative $m$, the reduced functional is the unique one taking the reduced positive generator to $1$. Thus the canonical map $\Gamma(s,\mathcal O_E(m))\otimes A_{E,n}\to\Gamma(s,A_{E,n}(m))$ is the isomorphism of free lines taking one generator to the other. This argument uses the rank-one bases, and makes no general assertion that sections commute with nonflat tensor. With $u=q^{-m}\in\mathbf Z_\ell^\times$, a pure tensor $x\otimes a$ satisfies $\operatorname{red}(F_m x\otimes a)=\operatorname{red}(ux\otimes a)=\bar u\,\operatorname{red}(x\otimes a)=F_m\operatorname{red}(x\otimes a)$. This is the required finite-reduction intertwining, including in ramified extensions and at $n=1$.

source.place: These actions commute with finite reduction; explicit generator and scalar calculation

proof.text: For $E$ the Weil structure is the image of the integral structure under scalar localization [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists], clause 4; the point transport and fiber are also the integral ones tensored with $E$ [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport, def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Thus the computed endomorphism is $q^{-m}\operatorname{id}$ on $\mathcal O_E e_m\otimes E$, and the integral-to-rational comparison is an isomorphism intertwining it. For a finite extension $E\subset E'$ the point-sections comparison [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] identifies the sections of integral scalar extension with $\Gamma(s,\mathcal O_E(m))\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_{E'}$, and after rationalizing identifies $H^0(s,E'(m))$ with $H^0(s,E(m))\otimes_E E'$. The common root system $e$ supplies the same generator after extension, including its tensor powers and duals, by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The scalar $q^{-m}$ has the same image under all these coefficient homomorphisms. On each pure tensor the intertwining equality is $(u x)\otimes b=u(x\otimes b)$, as in step 8. At $\Qlb$ take the common-stage class of these isomorphisms; the identity and composition compatibilities in [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] make the class independent of stage. Finally [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] defines $F$ by precisely the transport-then-Weil-structure composite used here, so the $E$ and $\Qlb$ operators are the stated global geometric Frobenius. Substituting $m=1$ and $m=-d$ gives $q^{-1}$ and $q^d$.
